competitiveAlternatives: Scroll District, Insider or HighApe and pick a night
Follow a few promoters on Instagram
Read Wild City or RA's India guides
uniqueAttributes: Curated, capped, RSVP-only Episodes (200-400 people) in house, disco, UK garage, breaks, drum & bass, jungle and dub techno; no commercial EDM
A national scene platform behind the nights: Discover (all underground events in one feed), artist profiles with booking, promoter listings, city and genre guides
Limited screen-printed apparel and pet streetwear with no restocks
Pet-friendly CCD x Social series and Cats Can Care
A distinct visual world (brutalist isometric cats, top-hat cat) and a founder who DJs and produces, with a ~150k-follower page
value: Fans: the good nights, with a crowd that listens, and the whole scene in one place
Artists: a listening room, real content and a profile that gets them booked
Venues and promoters: the right crowd and better spend
Buyers: pieces from a real scene, not merch
positioning.bestFitCustomer: 21-35 year-olds in Bengaluru (then Mumbai, Delhi, Goa) who choose nights by sound and crowd, buy limited streetwear, and often have a pet; plus the DJs who play for them.
positioning.marketCategory: Underground dance music culture brand and scene platform
positioning.statement: Cats Can Dance is India's underground dance music crew and scene platform: curated RSVP-only nights where the crowd listens, every underground event in one place, and limited drops from the people who live it.

motivations.name: A room that listens
motivations.insight: Fans pick nights by crowd as much as lineup; most rooms aren't there for the music

motivations.name: The sound
motivations.insight: Genre loyalists (house, garage, DnB, jungle, disco) want their genre done properly

motivations.name: Free, but you have to RSVP
motivations.insight: Free entry with a cap creates real urgency without discounting
proofPoints: Most Episodes are free with name on the door

motivations.name: Know what's on, everywhere
motivations.insight: Finding good underground nights across apps is a chore; one feed and a Monday email solves it
proofPoints: Discover pulls Skillbox, District, Insider, HighApe nightly

motivations.name: No restocks
motivations.insight: Streetwear buyers act on real scarcity and a scene story
proofPoints: No restocks on apparel or pet drops

motivations.name: Bring your pet
motivations.insight: Pet owners skip nights out; CCD x Social and pet streetwear are made for them
proofPoints: Cat bandanas and pet bucket hats

motivations.name: Play a room that listens, get booked
motivations.insight: DJs want an audience and content, not just a slot
proofPoints: Full set recording and photo/video assets
Profile with EPK, availability and booking

offers.name: RSVP + join the list
offers.hypothesis: Asking for email and WhatsApp at RSVP (with a reminder promise) grows the owned list faster than a standalone newsletter signup
offers.structure: RSVP form collects email and WhatsApp opt-in; 24h-before WhatsApp reminder; day-after recap with set recording
offers.risk: Form friction lowers RSVPs; keep it to name, email, WhatsApp, how you heard about us

offers.name: Episode drop
offers.hypothesis: A small apparel or pet drop announced at each Episode and sold to the list first converts better than standalone drops
offers.structure: List gets 24h early access; limited quantity; available at the Episode and online
offers.risk: Inventory risk if quantities are set too high

offers.name: Claim your profile
offers.hypothesis: Artists who claim profiles share them and bring their fans to Discover and Episodes
offers.structure: Outreach to every artist who has played or been scraped; shareable profile card
offers.risk: Low claim rate without personal outreach

offers.name: Points that pay out
offers.hypothesis: Turning on points redemption (e.g. a shop discount at 100 points) raises repeat RSVPs and first purchases
offers.structure: Redeem points for a shop discount code; show balance in the digest
offers.risk: Engineering time; the current 'coming soon' state hurts trust until it ships

channels.channel: Founder page (~150k) and CCD Instagram: daily music content, Episode and drop moments
channels.kpi: Shares, saves, follows to CCD, RSVPs from Instagram (HDYHAU)

channels.channel: Meta ads (Instagram first), broad, distinct concepts across motivations, optimised for RSVP/sign-up
channels.kpi: Cost per RSVP and cost per list sign-up
channels.cadence: From Episode announcement to the night; ~₹7,000/month

channels.channel: Boosts of the best organic posts (Reels and carousels)
channels.kpi: Cost per profile visit and RSVP
channels.cadence: Weekly, only posts beating the account median on shares/saves

channels.channel: Drop retargeting to site visitors and engagers
Email weekly digest + WhatsApp community and reminders
channels.kpi: RSVP rate from list, repeat attendance, drop revenue per recipient

channels.channel: Ticketing app listings (District, Insider, HighApe, SortMyScene, Skillbox)
Scene guides, genre pages and on-site event pages (SEO/GEO)
channels.kpi: AI-answer citations and organic visits to Discover
channels.cadence: Monthly guide updates; a page per event

channels.channel: Artist outreach to claim profiles; artists share their Episode content
channels.kpi: Profiles claimed, artist shares, RSVPs via artists (HDYHAU)

primaryMetric.name: Owned audience growth: new RSVPs + email + WhatsApp contacts per month, and cost per new contact
primaryMetric.target: Set after the first month of tracking; then sell out every Episode and every drop

tests.hypothesis: 'A room that listens' beats 'Free, but you have to RSVP' on cost per RSVP
tests.killRule: Pause a motivation at 2x the best cost after ₹1,500 spend

tests.hypothesis: Founder talking-head Reels beat designed statics
tests.killRule: Drop the losing format for the next Episode

tests.hypothesis: List-first early access sells a drop faster than an open launch
tests.killRule: Revert to open launches if early access doesn't beat it twice

risks: ₹10,000/month is small: Meta needs concentrated spend around each Episode to learn, so avoid splitting across many campaigns
If Episodes are infrequent, paid has nothing to point at; a fixed calendar matters more than budget
Platform leaks (no points redemption, offsite curated events, no reminders) waste paid traffic until fixed
Free RSVPs can no-show; track attendance, not just RSVPs
